question: Income of Amit in 2019 was ₹22,000. He gets an increment of 10% every year. What was his income (in ₹) in 2021?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the **successive percentage** formula or **multiplying factor** for 2 years.

Net increment = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%.

Income in 2021 = 22,000 × 121/100 = 26,620.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹26,620.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **Income (2019)** = ₹22,000, **Increment Rate** = 10% per annum, **Time Period** = 2 years (2019 to 2021).

**Formula Used:** Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c32d083023176cf8b997bbac1388d8bd1b23e9d732ffef92c952bf52af5217a.png] 

⇒ Income in 2020 = 22,000 + (10% of 22,000)

⇒ Income in 2020 = 22,000 + 2,200 = ₹24,200

⇒ Income in 2021 = 24,200 + (10% of 24,200)

⇒ Income in 2021 = 24,200 + 2,420 = ₹26,620

**∴ The correct answer is ₹26,620.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net effective change is (a + b + ab/100)%.

Multiplying Factor (MF)

For an x% increase, the multiplying factor is (1 + x/100). For 10% increase, MF = 1.1.

Depreciation

If the value decreases every year, the formula becomes Final Value = Initial Value × (1 − R/100)ⁿ.
